back: Memory directly accessed by the CPU: RAM and ROM.
Random access memory: volatile, read-write; holds the OS, programs and data in use.
Read only memory: non-volatile, read-only; holds the bootstrap (start-up instructions).
Loses its contents when the power is switched off (e.g. RAM).
Runs from ROM at switch-on, checks the hardware and loads the operating system from secondary storage into RAM.
ROM: permanent start-up instructions (RAM is empty at switch-on). RAM: changeable programs and data in use.
An area of secondary storage used as extra RAM when RAM is full; pages are moved between them.
Constant moving of pages between RAM and virtual memory, which makes the computer very slow.
Add more RAM so more programs and data fit at once.
